findings.description: __aexit__ discards the exception it receives and calls self.__exit__(None, None, None), so an exception raised inside an `async with` attempt is recorded as a successful result instead of a failure.
findings.rationale: Trigger: an `async with` retry attempt body raises, e.g. a ValueError from a network call. Mechanism: __aexit__ passes None for exc_type and exc_value, so the sync __exit__ takes the else branch and calls retry_state.set_result(None) rather than set_exception, and it returns None so the exception still propagates. Impact: the retry loop sees the attempt as successful, so it neither retries nor records the failure, and the exception escapes the retry logic. The sync AttemptManager path handles this correctly by passing the real exception info.
